thread:
sanjay: Hey folks, first-week onboarding question. I'm running an embeddings sweep from my laptop (~60k markdown files, ~900k tokens) using the hosted sandbox key and hit 429s after a bit. Error:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-ratelimit-type: token
retry-after: 30
```
Anyone know the fastest way to get a short bump (90m) so the full job can finish? Who should I ping? @infra or ops? :thinking:

slash-bot: You can use the internal Slack workflow `/sandbox-bump` to open a tracked request (recommended). The workflow asks for account id, token id (if known), total tokens, peak qps, duration, and cost center. It creates a ticket in ServiceDesk and notifies infra ops. Quick auto-approvals for <=3M tokens & <=4h.

amelia: If the workflow is slow for you I can also hand out an ephemeral token (1.5h) scoped to embeddings-only. DM me the time window & cost center. Ephemeral tokens are auditable.

devx-julie: Another pattern: upload sanitized payload to the internal tmp S3 and request an ops-run to execute the batch from a reserved account. That avoids touching your sandbox quota. We do this a lot for onboarding runs.

security-matt: Security reminder: never paste tokens in channels. If the data contains customer PII, redact first and add tag `sensitive:yes` on the S3 object. If unsure, DM me and I'll advise.

ops-lee: Ops will need the cost center and approximate calls/sec. Also say whether it's streaming or batch.

sanjay: Cool, I'll try the `/sandbox-bump` workflow now. Cost center: "search-poc". Window requested tomorrow 07:30-09:00 PDT. Estimated total tokens ~920k, peak ~8 qps, batch job. Thanks all! :raised_hands:
